text:
BERT4Rec uses learned absolute positional embeddings, truncates long histories, and predicts from an appended MASK token’s representation ([original paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1904.06690)). Consequently, a controlled deletion probe should first construct the exact baseline inference tensor, reserving space for MASK, then select equally sized recent and older subsets within that original visible window. Recommended control, inferred from these mechanics: remove selected interactions from attention while retaining surviving tokens’ original position IDs and the original MASK position; do not backfill from history outside the window. Use padding with a correct attention mask for deleted slots, rather than extra MASK tokens. Read the appended MASK’s actual position; with left padding or interior holes, nonpadding-count minus one is incorrect. Compacting and repadding can be reported separately, but measures deletion plus positional changes.

Freeze candidate eligibility using each user’s original complete observed history, including interactions outside the visible window and those deleted by the probe. Deleted items remain seen and excluded. For full-catalog recommendations, reuse the same unseen-item pool; for pinned validation, reuse the exact target and 99 unique negatives, without resampling or modifying the evaluator. Candidate sampling can change metric values and model comparisons ([Krichene and Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)); freezing candidates is therefore an experimental control inferred from that finding. Compare paired score, rank, or HR@10 changes for identical users and deletion counts, with dropout disabled. Interpret results as sensitivity to removing visible evidence under fixed positions and eligibility, rather than causal evidence about user preferences.
